backlogItem: MIRROR the piece-square tables per color
change: getPieceValueSum now mirrors the board index (rank r -> 7-r) for black pieces, so Black reads the piece-square tables from its own perspective instead of White's. evaluate() gains a `mirror` flag (default true) and negamax() an optional `evaluateFn` so the harness can A/B new vs legacy from a single eval source.
reason: Net-positive and non-regressing across ~700 seeded games at depths 2 and 3, and a genuine correctness fix (Black's positional evaluation was vertically inverted). Color-symmetry unit tests confirm evaluate() is now side-symmetric. Bundle well under the 45KB brotli limit.

change: negamax default leaf evaluator is now quiescentEval: at the search horizon it resolves pending captures via a stand-pat negamax (MVV-LVA ordered, delta-pruned with a 200cp promotion-aware margin, self-check-filtered, capture-promotions auto-queened) before scoring. Fixes the horizon effect where the static evaluate() was taken mid-exchange and mis-counted material. Harness updated: newEval=quiescentEval, legacyEval=static mirrored evaluate() (the previous accepted engine), isolating the quiescence contribution. En passant and check-evasions are intentionally omitted (standard qsearch simplification); mate is still scored by negamax at its own nodes.
review: adversarial subagent review: all 9 correctness checks pass; delta-pruning soundness fuzz-verified (0 mismatches across ~30k legal positions); self-check/pin filter and sign convention confirmed empirically
reason: Large, robust strength gain that is also a genuine correctness improvement (eliminates horizon-effect blunders). Non-regressing and strongly net-positive across 560 seeded games from varied openings, both colors: 88.9% at depth 2 (400 games) and 93.1% at depth 3 (160 games), across two seeds each, with near-zero losses (11L/6L). Two new unit tests pin the behavior (declines a poisoned capture, grabs a winning one). Bundle 6.81KB brotli, far under the 45KB limit.

change: Added a pawn-structure term (doubled -12/extra file, isolated -14, passed-pawn bonus rising by rank) as pawnStructureDelta(board) = White-minus-Black, layered onto the static eval via a new evaluateFull() used as the production quiescence leaf. evaluate() itself was left structure-free; the quiescence stand-pat gained a pawnStructure flag so the harness could A/B new=quiescence+structure (quiescentEval->evaluateFull) vs legacy=quiescence-only (quiescentEvalNoStructure, the experiment #2 engine). Correctness pinned by exact-value + color-symmetry unit tests.

depth3_afterOffByOneFix.note: Fixed an off-by-one that zeroed the 7th-rank passed bonus (PASSED_BONUS[7]=0) and peaked it at the 6th; raising the 7th-rank bonus to 130 made depth-3 strictly worse (41.9%->36.9%), a clean monotonic trend: more passed-pawn weight => weaker play.

rootCause: The passed-pawn incentive makes this shallow-search engine chase/advance passers it cannot convert within the horizon, conceding material and tactics that the structure-blind baseline then punishes. The effect is depth-dependent (neutral at depth 2, clear regression at depth 3) and worsens monotonically as the passer bonus grows, so it is the eval term steering the search wrong, not a tuning accident. Color symmetry and starting-position=0 were unit-verified, ruling out an asymmetry bug.
reason: Fails the self-play NON-REGRESSION gate at depth 3 under two independent tunings (41.9% then 36.9% over 160 games/seed). All other gate checks (typecheck/lint/format/tests/build/size 7.06KB) passed, but per the gate a strength regression must be fixed or fully reverted; the one available fix made it worse, so the change was fully reverted to the experiment #2 engine and only this ledger entry is committed. Lesson for future runs: a naive pawn-structure term (especially the passed-pawn bonus) is counterproductive for this engine at the UI's search depths. Revisit only with much smaller weights, gated on the pawn being safely advanceable, or after a search-depth / king-safety improvement — and always validate at depth 3+, not just depth 2.
